open_issues: CROSS-PACKAGE (carried forward, now unblocked): nothing in the shipped tree starts the background work. The B2 screens/shell package must call IClockGuard.StartAsync(now, InvokeAsync) and IReminderScheduler.Start(ticker, InvokeAsync) — passing the renderer's ComponentBase.InvokeAsync as the BackgroundPassDispatcher, which is the whole point of the new parameter — and must call IReminderScheduler.Stop() and IClockGuard.Stop() on sign-out/lock. Until it does, «مهمة خلفية كل دقيقة» and «يشغّل ClockCheckService عند التشغيل وكل 10 دقائق» do not happen in the running product.

CROSS-PACKAGE: ClockCheckTrigger.Import still has no caller. «وعند الاستيراد» is satisfied only when the sync package calls IClockGuard.CheckAsync(ClockCheckTrigger.Import, now, importedDeviceTimestamps).
CROSS-PACKAGE: HealthCard carries no per-card timestamp; the W12 «آخر فحص 10:24» line must come from HealthReport.CheckedAt, which applies to the whole run.

CROSS-PACKAGE (from the review's consumability notes, unchanged): W08's KPI subtitles must be composed by the screen from IAttentionService.GetThresholdsAsync, and W08's per-type inner tabs must be derived from IAttentionService.GetAllAsync — NOT from AttentionSnapshot.NeedsActionToday, which is capped at 200 while Counts is uncapped.

The four Windows probes (Word, WIA scanner, disk, WebView2 runtime) still have no unit tests: tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests targets net10.0 and cannot reference the net10.0-windows host, and adding a test project would require editing Wakeel.slnx. All four ran for real during the host boot.

HealthService.PersistAsync issues one small query per component (11 per run) to find the newest stored snapshot. A single grouped query would be cheaper, but GroupBy+First does not translate reliably on SQLite; at one run per 15 minutes the cost is negligible.
notes:
All findings addressed; chain green: `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Core` (0 warnings / 0 errors, TreatWarningsAsErrors on) -> `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests` (323/323 passed, 17 s; was 304) -> `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop` (0/0).

HIGH — background timers writing to the shared WakeelDb. Took the review's third shape, the only one that actually works here (a fresh DI scope would hand back the same WakeelDb, since the host registers it as a factory over the singleton AccountSession.Db). New src/Wakeel.Core/Services/BackgroundPass.cs defines `public delegate Task BackgroundPassDispatcher(Func<Task> pass)` — deliberately the exact shape of ComponentBase.InvokeAsync, so the shell passes the method group straight in — plus `BackgroundPass.Inline` for a caller that owns the session alone. `IClockGuard.StartAsync(DateTime, BackgroundPassDispatcher, CancellationToken)` and `IReminderScheduler.Start(IMinuteTicker, BackgroundPassDispatcher)` now REQUIRE one (no default value, ArgumentNullException on null, so no caller can drift into the unsafe path by omission), and every pass goes through it — including ClockGuard's startup check, which by the time the shell runs it is already contending with a rendering screen. The contract is documented on both interface members, on the delegate, and in both classes' remarks. Tests: the dispatcher is used and the row is written (StartAsync_RunsEveryCheckThroughTheDispatcherTheShellSupplied, EveryPassRunsThroughTheDispatcher...), null is refused on both, and APassAndAScreensQuery_ShareTheSessionSafelyWhenBothGoThroughTheShellsDispatcher runs 20 scheduler passes concurrently with 20 UI-style query batches on the same WakeelDb through one gate and asserts nothing throws (the test drives the tick directly, so the ticker's swallowing catch cannot hide a failure).

MEDIUM — the ticker silently discarding a second Start. Did both remedies. TimeProviderMinuteTicker.Start now rebinds: a new private StopCore() cancels and disposes the existing CTS and timer inside the lock before the new timer is created, and the XML doc states that a second Start REPLACES the callback. ClockGuard.StartAsync got the same treatment (it had the identical early-return). IMinuteTicker is now AddScoped instead of AddSingleton, so the tick dies with the session that started it instead of outliving it undisposed. New tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests/MinuteTickerTests.cs with a ManualTimeProvider whose timers fire only on demand: Start(a) then Start(b) ticks b and never a, leaves exactly one live timer (and none after Stop), and a tick that throws does not stop the next one.

LOW — off-thread events. IBadgeService.Changed and IClockGuard.StateChanged now carry a <remarks> saying the handler may arrive off the renderer's context and that a Blazor subscriber must marshal through ComponentBase.InvokeAsync.

LOW — the 1440-minute reminder horizon. MaxLeadMinutes(int) is gone; MaxLeadMinutesAsync reads MAX(reminder_minutes) over the planned meetings and appointments the pass is about to read anyway and takes the larger of that and the settings default. Two new tests fire a 2880-minute (two-day) meeting and appointment exactly when due, and assert nothing a minute earlier.

LOW — UTC vs local day in AttentionWindow. AttentionWindow.For now takes an optional TimeZoneInfo, derives the day from the local date and converts the late/near cutoffs back to UTC; the struct carries LocalToday and Zone, and DaysLate measures both sides in local days. Added a shared StartOfLocalDay helper with a DST-gap guard (Palestine starts summer time at midnight, so that one night's midnight does not exist and the raw conversion would have thrown) and pointed ReadTodayMeetingsAsync at it too. New AttentionWindowTests fixes a UTC+3 zone and asserts the same row classifies identically at 01:00 and 09:00 local, that LateCutoff is local midnight (21:00Z, not 00:00Z), and that a record due later today is Near on both readings. I checked the old code against these: it returned Near at 01:00 and Late at 09:00, so the tests are real regressions guards, not tautologies.

LOW — health_snapshots growth. CheckAsync's persist path moved into PersistAsync: a card is stored only when its status, message or action differs from the newest stored snapshot for that component, so the table becomes a list of changes rather than a transcript of every quarter-hour re-check; and when anything is written, snapshots older than the new HealthService.SnapshotRetention (90 days) are dropped with ExecuteDeleteAsync in the same save. Three tests: a no-change re-run adds nothing, a scanner going missing adds exactly one row with the new status, and an ancient row is pruned.

LOW — untrue health messages. New CoreAr.HealthVaultUnreadable («تعذّر فحص الخزنة الآن») and CoreAr.HealthModelsUnreadable («تعذّر فحص مجلد النماذج الآن») are returned from the catch blocks; «غير موجود» now only comes from the Directory.Exists branch. Both strings are in CoreAr.cs, so the existing no-jargon/no-server test covers them.

LOW — sync disagreement. AttentionService.ReadSyncStateAsync now filters d.RevokedAt == null, matching HealthService.CheckSyncAsync. New test seeds a revoked PC synced 5 minutes ago and a live phone synced 6 hours ago and asserts W08 reports the phone.

LOW — the shekel sign. Checked design/exports/preview/light/W/W08 (viewed once): the phone-expense rows render «₪ 42.50» with the sign leading. Money.Shekels now emits "₪ {amount}" under InvariantCulture, with a remark explaining that ₪ is a bidi currency terminator so writing it first is what puts it on the side the mockup shows. AttentionItem.NumberAr's doc now states the <bdi>/unicode-bidi: isolate obligation (item 55). New MoneyTests cover the format and assert no Arabic-Indic digits.

Re-verified after the changes: performance unchanged — [b2-services] rows=10000 seed=1453ms attention-snapshot=48ms badges-refresh=52ms attention-counts=41ms budget=200ms (was 46/47/39), so the per-row local-date conversion in DaysLate costs nothing measurable. Host re-checked: Wakeel.Desktop.exe on port 9333 with an empty temp data folder, /json/version answered (Edg/153.0.4234.32), /json/list reported /first-run, CDP JPEG captured and looked at — W02 renders intact in dark RTL with the three-step indicator on step 2, the setup-file drop zone, the package-password field with its reveal eye, «فحص الحزمة» and the footer «الوكيل v0.21 — 16/09/2026 21:06»; no server/port/internet/database wording. Host log held one INF startup line and no errors; process killed, 0 Wakeel.Desktop.exe remaining. No files outside src/Wakeel.Core, tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests and docs/build/progress/b2-services.md were touched (no Desktop DI change was needed this round), and no NuGet package was added.
